t: Match Alphanumerical Pattern in Matrix I — Brute Force with Consistency Checks
o: Slide the pattern over every possible top-left corner of `board` and verify the match: digit cells must equal board values exactly; each letter maps to one unique digit, different letters to different digits, consistently across the whole pattern. Return the first (row-major) match or [-1,-1]. Sizes ≤ 50 mean 2500 placements × 2500 cells = ~6M checks — brute force is intended here.
k: Two maps enforce bijection: letter→digit and digit→letter.

a.n: Approach 1: Sliding window with bidirectional mapping
a.i: For each placement, walk pattern cells; maintain `letterToDigit` and `digitToLetter` maps. Any conflict (digit mismatch, letter remapping, or digit reuse by another letter) rejects the placement immediately.
s: Iterate top-left corners in row-major order (guarantees lexicographically smallest answer).
For each cell, check digit equality or letter-consistency via two maps.
Return the first corner passing all cells; else [-1,-1].
a.t: O(R·C·P·Q) — every placement checked cell by cell, ~6M ops at max sizes
a.sp: O(1) — two tiny maps reused per placement

w: Iterating corners in row-major order automatically satisfies the tie-breaking rule — no explicit comparison needed. Pitfall: forgetting the digit→letter direction lets two letters silently map to the same digit (example 3). The hard version (#3079) has much larger inputs and needs 2-D hashing / string matching.
